steps.body: A CUBE root asks: what number, multiplied by itself three times, gives this result? ∛27 = 3 since 3³ = 27. Perfect cubes to know: 1, 8, 27, 64, 125 (from 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³, 5³).
Complete a cube with volume 64 and read the missing edge length.

widget.prompt: The cube is 4 units wide and 4 units high. Extend its remaining edge until the volume is 64 cubic units.

commonBuilds.feedback: A 2 × 4 × 4 prism has volume 32, so its three edges are not all 4 yet.
A 3 × 4 × 4 prism has volume 48. Extend the remaining edge one more unit.

widget.successFeedback: The edges are 4, 4, and 4, so the cube holds 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 unit cubes. Therefore ∛64 = 4.
widget.lowFeedback: The volume is below 64. Extend the free edge while the other two edges stay at 4.
widget.highFeedback: The volume is above 64. Shorten the free edge until all three edge lengths are 4.

predict.prompt: What does ∛64 ask you to find?

options.label: An edge used three times to make a volume of 64

predict.reveal: A cube root finds the edge length of a cube with the given volume. Since 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, the cube's edge and ∛64 are both 4.

steps.body: Here's the twist: solving x³ = p has only ONE real solution, even when p is negative! A negative number cubed STAYS negative ((−2)³ = −8), so negatives and positives never collide the way they do with squaring — no ± needed for cube roots.

explanationVariants: 3³ = 27, so x³ = 27 has the single solution x = 3.

commonBuilds.feedback: Cube equations don't need ±: (−3)³ = −27, not 27 — only +3 works.
Cube equations don't need ±: (−3)³ = −27, not 27 — only +3 works.
9³ is far more than 27 — not a solution.
That's half of 27, not a cube root — check 3³ = 27 instead.

widget.missFeedback: A cube root keeps its sign — only 3³ = 27; −3 cubes to −27.
widget.successFeedback: Right — 3³ = 27, and cube equations have just one real solution.

options.label: x = −2
options.feedback: Right — (−2)³ = −8, and only one number cubes to −8.

options.label: x = 2
options.feedback: 2³ = 8, not −8 — the sign matters here, unlike with squares.

options.label: x = 2 or x = −2
options.feedback: Only −2 works: 2³ = 8 (positive), so 2 does NOT solve x³=−8.

options.label: No real solution
options.feedback: There IS a real solution — negative numbers have real cube roots, unlike square roots of negatives.

steps.body: A cube equation with an extra step.
explanationVariants: (x+1)³ = −27 means x+1 = −3 (since only −3 cubes to −27), so x = −3 − 1 = −4.
Cube-root first to get x+1 = −3, then finish the linear step: x = −4.

commonBuilds.feedback: That's x+1 = −3, but you still need to isolate x: −3 − 1 = −4. (x+1)³ = −27 means x = −4, not −3.
That drops the negative sign: (2+1)³ = 27, not −27. Cubing preserves the sign, so x+1 must be −3, which gives x = −4.
Cube equations don't need ±: (2+1)³ = 27, not −27 — only x = −4 works.

widget.missFeedback: Cubing preserves the sign: (x+1)³ = −27 means x+1 = −3, so x = −3 − 1 = −4.

steps.body: Translate words into the equation first.
explanationVariants: "Multiplied by itself three times" means cubed: translating to x³ = 216 gives x = 6.
6×6×6 = 216, and cube equations have just one real solution: 6.

widget.prompt: A number, multiplied by itself three times, equals 216. What is the number?

commonErrors.feedback: 72 comes from dividing by 3, but cubing means multiplying by itself THREE TIMES (6×6×6), not dividing. 6×6×6 = 216.
108 is half of 216, not a cube root. 6×6×6 = 216, so the number is 6.

steps.body: Cube root of a negative, reinforced.

commonErrors.feedback: Check the sign — 4³ = 64 (positive), but we need −64, so the answer must be negative: −4.
That divides −64 by 4 — a cube root isn't division. (−4)³ = −64, so ∛(−64) = −4.

steps.body: Apply it: volume back to edge length.
explanationVariants: Volume = edge³, so 343 = edge³ means the edge is 7 inches, since 7×7×7 = 343.
7³ = 343 — translating the box's volume back to its edge length gives 7 inches.

widget.prompt: A cube-shaped box has a volume of 343 cubic inches. What is the length of one edge, in inches?

commonErrors.feedback: 1029 multiplies 343 by 3, but cubing means finding what number times ITSELF three times gives 343 — not multiplying 343 by 3. 7×7×7 = 343, so the edge is 7 inches.
171.5 is half of 343, not a cube root. 7×7×7 = 343, so the edge is 7 inches.

widget.fallbackFeedback: 7×7×7 = 343, so the edge length is 7 inches.

steps.body: Cube equations have exactly ONE real solution — negatives included, no ± needed.
takeaways: ∛p asks: what number cubed gives p?
A negative number cubed stays negative, so cube roots of negatives are real, unlike square roots of negatives.
x³ = p always has exactly one real solution, unlike x² = p's two.
